quarterly_data.signal: PFO Doug Caring: Q3 FY2026 (ended February) was the first quarter in over 15 years where both organic total revenue and organic non-GAAP EPS grew at 20% or better in USD. Mike Cecilia: cloud applications revenue up 11% in constant currency to an annualized run rate of $16.1 billion (Fusion ERP +14%, SCM +15%, HCM +15%, NetSuite +11%); cloud applications deferred revenue up 14%; over 2,000 customers went live in Q3 and well over 1,000 AI agents are already delivered inside Oracle applications.
quarterly_data.figure: organic revenue and non-GAAP EPS growth 20% or better; cloud applications +11% cc, run rate $16.1 billion; over 2,000 go-lives

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Clay McGouyrk: multicloud database revenue grew 531% year over year and AI infrastructure revenue grew 243% year over year; both have demand that exceeds supply. 'Demand for AI infrastructure, both GPU and CPU, continues to exceed supply. This is directly visible in our $553 billion RPO.' Multicloud regions: 33 live with Microsoft, 14 live with Google; AWS went from two regions live at the start of Q3 to eight at the exit, with 22 AWS regions live expected by the exit of Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: multicloud database revenue +531%; AI infrastructure revenue +243%; eight AWS regions exiting Q3, 22 AWS regions exiting Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Clay McGouyrk on capacity: through partners Oracle has secured more than 10 gigawatts of power and data capacity coming online over the next three years, and greater than 90% of that capacity is fully funded through partners (the remainder planned to finish this month). Supply chain has more suppliers and deeper relationships; Oracle tripled its manufacturing sites and increased rack output by 4x in the last year. In Q3 Oracle delivered more than 400 megawatts to customers, with 90% of committed capacity delivered on or ahead of schedule.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 10 gigawatts secured over the next three years (greater than 90% funded through partners); rack output 4x; more than 400 megawatts delivered in Q3

quarterly_data.signal: Funding model: Clay McGouyrk said Oracle has signed more than $29 billion of contracts since the prior call across multiple customers using bring-your-own-hardware and upfront customer payments, which lets Oracle expand without negative cash flow; this is in addition to other deals signed in the quarter. Doug Caring: in February Oracle announced it would raise up to $50 billion in debt and equity (no additional bonds beyond that in calendar 2026) and raised $30 billion within days via investment-grade bonds and mandatory convertible preferred stock; the at-the-market equity portion has not started. FY2027 capex will be discussed after fiscal year-end, with capex increasingly 'uncoupled' from Oracle's own capital requirements.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $29 billion BYOH/prepaid contracts; up to $50 billion financing, $30 billion raised

quarterly_data.signal: AI infrastructure profitability (Clay McGouyrk): gross margin on the AI capacity delivered in Q3 was 32%, above the 30% guidance; the 30% to 40% gross-margin range on accelerators continues to hold. Adjacent services (general-purpose compute, storage, load balancing, security) are typically 10% to 20% of total AI data center spend at higher margins, and multicloud database runs at 60% to 80% margins. The only drag on profitability is the volume of capacity under construction at once; delivered capacity is already contracted at a profitable rate.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 AI capacity gross margin 32%; 30% to 40% range holds; adjacent services 10% to 20% of spend

quarterly_data.signal: Accelerator mix and inference: Clay McGouyrk said Oracle offers 'the latest in accelerators, from the most recent NVIDIA and AMD options to emerging designs from companies like Cerebras and PowerCharm.' On inference latency he said the problem is the type of hardware rather than data center location, citing GROQ, Cerebras and Positron, and pointed to an NVIDIA announcement at GTC the following week; this lets Oracle site data centers where power is abundant and land is plentiful.

OCI wins named by Mike Cecilia in Q3: Lockheed Martin selected OCI high-performance compute to scale AI; Rhombus selected OCI Compute, Networking and Storage for AI video; Claro Brazil selected OCI Alloy for Sovereign AI. Management said sovereign and Alloy pipeline is increasing worldwide, deliverable from three racks to 500 racks with full OCI services.
